title: French burglar used ChatGPT to locate Canberra home with luxury goods

By Harry Frost

Topic:Courts

The men pleaded guilty to stealing an array of expensive pieces including handbags, rings and jewellery.  (Supplied)

One of the four French nationals who stole a haul of luxury goods from a Canberra home last year used artificial intelligence to locate their target.

The four men have pleaded guilty to charges of aggravated burglary and joint commission theft, but their lawyers have disputed the total value of the stolen items.

The ACT Supreme Court will set a date for the mens' sentencing next week.

Court documents have revealed how a French burglar used artificial intelligence and images posted to social media to locate a home containing luxury goods in Australia.

He, along with three other French nationals, stole a haul of designer jewellery, handbags and watches from a home in Canberra's south in October last year, before being arrested at a fast food outlet in Sydney just days later.

Ilyes Abdelkader, Mohamed Abdelkader, Mohamed Naimi and Antoni Voisin pleaded guilty to charges of aggravated burglary and joint commission theft in March, but their lawyers disputed the total value of the stolen items.

When charges were laid in December, police said some of the stolen goods — including designer handbags — had been recovered from a short-term rental property in Wentworthville, Sydney, while other items were located by French authorities.

The victims claim a Richard Mille rm88 (Smiley) watch was among the items stolen from a Canberra home in October. (Supplied: Richard Mille)

But several items the victims claimed were still missing, including a Richard Mille RM88 (Smiley) watch worth $5 million, were yet to be returned.

In a hearing in the ACT Supreme Court today, prosecutors tendered an agreed statement of facts, which revised the total value of the goods down from its original figure of $10 million to just under $2 million, with some of the items still unrecovered.

"The prosecution cannot prove beyond reasonable doubt that these [unreturned] items were genuine," the facts read.

"The victims have not been able to produce any documentation such as receipts, proof of purchase, transaction records, or certificates to prove the authenticity of those items."

A Patek Philippe 5711 40th anniversary watch similar to the one stolen from a Canberra home. (Supplied)

The document also noted how one of the victims had posted images of the luxury goods on Instagram.

Ilyes Abdelkader used artificial intelligence to determine a cherry blossom tree in one of those images was usually found in Canberra, while another image contained Black Mountain tower — also in the ACT.

The victim had also posted photos of their backyard containing a swimming pool and tennis court.

NSW police arrested the four men at Wentworthville KFC in Sydney on October 19. (ABC News: Liam Patrick)

Mr Abdelkader used ChatGPT to search for suburbs in Canberra with tennis courts and pools and located the home.

He and the three other men then flew from Thailand to Sydney on October 7.

The group broke into the home in Canberra a few days later, while the victims were out, using tree trunks to smash a window and gaining access to a safe which the victims thought had been left locked.

Police allege the men travelled to Australia to rob a Canberra home.

The men later used a freight service to send some of the now-recovered belongings to France.

They were arrested at a KFC in Wentworthville, Sydney, on October 19 and have been in custody since.

The ACT Supreme Court will set a date for their sentencing next week.

Court documents note goods valued at $915,000 have been returned, while items with an agreed value of more than $1 million are still outstanding.
